**Finding submitted: deviation (rule IP).**

- **What's wrong:** Article III (p0048) vests all right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology *and all Intellectual Property Rights* in Licensor. Because "Intellectual Property Rights" expressly includes "all additions, improvements and accessions" (p0015) and "Derivative Work" captures any modification incorporating the platform (p0005), the bespoke front end and customization work we commission **and pay for** under Article VII(b) (p0087) end up owned by Licensor — with no assignment to us and no perpetual licence back. Our only rights are the non-exclusive, Field-of-Use-limited licence that expires with the 36-month term (renewal at Licensor's option). There is also no ownership provision for our data.
- **Why it fails the fallback:** the fallback requires at minimum a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables; nothing here survives termination.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** a single inserted paragraph after Article III giving us ownership of deliverables developed specifically for and paid for by us, preserving Licensor's pre-existing platform IP with a perpetual licence to it where embedded, confirming our retention of all rights in Licensee Data, and excluding joint ownership. The comment offers the fallback (licence instead of assignment) if Licensor resists assigning derivatives of its platform.
